source1: Richard M. Eaton, The Rise of Islam and the Bengal Frontier, 1204-1760, University of California Press 1993 (Introduction) - https://publishing.cdlib.org/ucpressebooks/view?docId=ft067n99v9&brand=ucpress
source2: Abdul Karim, 'Islam Khan Chisti' and 'Bara-Bhuiyans, The', Banglapedia, Asiatic Society of Bangladesh - https://en.banglapedia.org/index.php/Islam_Khan_Chisti ; https://en.banglapedia.org/index.php/Bara-Bhuiyans,_The ; Britannica 'Mughal dynasty' - https://www.britannica.com/topic/Mughal-dynasty
notes: Islam Khan Chishti subdued all Bhuiyans incl. Musa Khan by end 1611. Mughals a Muslim dynasty with Persian records. Bhuiyan chiefs mixed, leaders Muslim; Eaton: Bengal's Muslim majority emerged later under Mughals, so population A kept with caution.

source1: David Robinson, Chiefs and Clerics: Abdul Bokar Kan and Futa Toro, 1853-1891, Clarendon Press (Oxford) 1975, Preface - https://webpulaaku.site/defte/david_robinson/chiefs_clerics/preface.html
source2: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Concordat of 1801' - https://www.britannica.com/event/Concordat-of-1801 ; EBSCO Research Starters, 'Louis Faidherbe' - https://www.ebsco.com/research-starters/history/louis-faidherbe
notes: Robinson calls Futa Toro an Islamic state; Faidherbe split it into French client states 1858-59, full annexation only by 1891. Second Empire kept the Concordat-recognized Catholic church; Faidherbe respected Islam but French rulers never adopted it.

source1: M. Arunachalam, The Kalabhras in the Pandiya Country and Their Impact on the Life and Letters There, University of Madras 1979 - https://www.tamildigitallibrary.in/admin/assets/book/TVA_BOK_0019058_The_Kalabhras_in_the_Pandiya_country.pdf
source2: 'Buddhadatta and his contributions to the History of Tamil Nadu', Journal of Tamil Peraivu (University of Malaya) 7(2), DOI 10.22452/JTP.vol7no2.8 - https://tamilperaivu.um.edu.my/article/view/15513
notes: Arunachalam: Kalabhras Jain in some places, Buddhist in others, rejects Saiva claims; Velvikudi plates say they seized Brahmin grants. Buddhadatta's Pali works under Kalabhra Achyutavikranta. No evidence of Hindu adoption. Writing inferred. Evidence thin.

Concordat of 1801 recognized Catholicism as France's chief religion; Napoleon consecrated by Pius VII in 1804. Napoleon annexed the Papal States 1809, Pius excommunicated the invaders and was imprisoned. Both Catholic.

source2: C. E. Bosworth, 'Ala al-Din Abu'l-Fath Mohammad', Encyclopaedia Iranica I/7, 1984 - https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/ala-al-din-abul-fath-mohammad-b
notes: Qarakhanids were Hanafi Sunni Muslims; Western khanate ended 1212 when Khwarazmshah Muhammad sacked Samarqand and killed Othman and kin. Muhammad Muslim, later opportunistic pro-Shii anti-caliph policy, still same tradition.

source1: Mohammed Hassen, The Oromo of Ethiopia, 1500-1850: with special emphasis on the Gibe region, PhD thesis, SOAS University of London 1983 - https://eprints.soas.ac.uk/29226
source2: Jan Zahorik, 'Iyasu V of Ethiopia (1913-1916): perilous traitor or a true modernizer?', University of West Bohemia - https://otik.zcu.cz/bitstream/11025/11847/1/Zahorik.pdf ; Temesgen Lemesa, The Oromo of Gommaa, 1880s-1991, thesis, Jimma University - https://repository.ju.edu.et/handle/123456789/6402
notes: Gibe states, incl. Gomma, were the leading Oromo centre of Islamic learning; Menelik of Shewa annexed them, direct rule from 1886. Ethiopian state privileged the Orthodox Church, Muslims second-class; no adoption of Islam.

source2: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, 'Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas' and 'Group of Monuments at Hampi' - https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1670 ; https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/241
notes: Hoysalas ruled to c. 1346 and were succeeded by Vijayanagar; Hoysala temples are Hindu (Jain minority). Vijayanagar fostered reconstruction of Hindu life and is called the last great Hindu kingdom. Same tradition.
